name: DCOUNT
description: DCOUNT counts the cells containing numbers in a specified field of the database records that match the given criteria.
tldr: Counts numeric values in a database column for rows that meet the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to count, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Yield") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and one or more condition rows; only matching records are counted.

basicExample.description: Count numeric Yield values for apple trees taller than 10
basicExample.explanation: The criteria A9:B10 (Tree=Apple, Height>10) matches two rows, and both have numeric Yield values, so the count is 2.

advancedExamples.title: Count a column with blank or text cells
advancedExamples.scenario: A field that mixes numbers and text
advancedExamples.description: If the chosen field contained a text label in one matching row, DCOUNT would exclude it because only numbers are counted.
advancedExamples.explanation: The Tree field holds text, not numbers, so DCOUNT returns 0 even though two rows match. DCOUNTA would count them instead.

advancedExamples.title: Count with a single condition
advancedExamples.scenario: Count all apple-tree records with numeric Yield
advancedExamples.explanation: Three apple rows exist (Yield 14, 10, 6), all numeric, so the count is 3.

howItWorks: DCOUNT filters the database to rows matching the criteria, then counts how many of those rows contain a numeric value in the specified field column. Empty cells and text in the field are not counted.

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row, e.g. A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up criteria
howToSteps.text: Place criteria headers and values in a separate range, e.g. A9:B10.

limitations: Counts only numeric cells; text and blank cells in the field are ignored.
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.
If you need to count non-numeric entries, use DCOUNTA.

commonErrors.cause: The chosen field holds text, or no rows matched the criteria.
commonErrors.fix: Use a numeric field, or switch to DCOUNTA for non-numeric entries.

commonErrors.cause: The field was an unquoted column name.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the field name in quotes, e.g. "Yield", or use the column index.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DCOUNT works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and behavior.

faq.question: Does DCOUNT count text values?
faq.answer: No. Only numeric values in the field are counted. Use DCOUNTA to count any non-blank cell.

faq.question: What does DCOUNT return if nothing matches?
faq.answer: It returns 0, because no numeric cells met the criteria.

faq.question: How is DCOUNT different from COUNTIF?
faq.answer: DCOUNT filters a multi-column database by a full criteria range, while COUNTIF applies a single condition to one range.
